activities.title: Explore Correlation
activities.instruction: Adjust the relationship strength and observe how correlation changes.

content.concept: Correlation measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two numerical variables.

activities.title: Anatomy of a Regression Line
activities.instruction: Explore the components of a simple linear regression equation.

content.concept: A simple linear regression model estimates a target variable using a predictor and represents the relationship with an equation such as y = mx + b.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The input variable used to explain or predict the target.
The actual outcome variable being studied.
Indicates how much the predicted target changes for a one-unit change in the predictor.
The predicted value of y when x equals zero.
The value predicted by the regression model.

activities.title: Build the Regression Workflow
activities.instruction: Arrange the steps into a logical regression workflow.

content.concept: Regression analysis involves preparing data, selecting variables, training a model, evaluating predictions, and interpreting the results.

goal: 3. Split the Data into Training and Testing Sets

activities.title: Correlation or Causation?
activities.instruction: Choose whether each statement describes association or establishes causation.

content.concept: Correlation shows that variables are associated, while causation requires evidence that changes in one variable produce changes in another.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Ice cream sales and swimming activity increase together → Correlation
A study randomly assigns a treatment and observes its effect → Evidence of causation
Umbrella sales and rainfall increase together → Correlation
Two variables move together because of a third variable → Possible confounding relationship
config.answer: Ice cream sales and swimming activity increase together → Correlation
